changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 7 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/3917-retire-action-condition-branch.md`

- names `content/docs/core/enhanced-actions.mdx` → `content/docs/core/enhanced-actions.mdx` — edited by this change

  > - `ActionCondition` is removed from `@object-ui/types` (and from the barrel export). - `ActionSchema.condition` is retyped to the predicate the runtime actually honours: `boolean | string | { dialect?: string; source: string }` — the same three arms `ActionRunner`'s own `ActionDef.condition` carries, and the same vocabulary `visible` and `disabled` use. - `ActionConditionSchema` is removed from `@object-ui/types/zod` (and from the zod barrel); the `condition` key now validates against that predicate union. - The two teaching sites (`content/docs/core/enhanced-actions.mdx` Conditional Execution, `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` ActionSchema table) are rewritten to the live vocabulary: `condition` is a gate; a branch is expressed as separate actions with mutually exclusive `condition`s.

### `.changeset/6169-chatbot-authoring-face-type.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `showTimestamp`, `userAvatarUrl`, `userAvatarFallback`, `assistantAvatarUrl`, `assistantAvatarFallback`, `maxHeight` — display fields. - `autoResponse`, `autoResponseText`, `autoResponseDelay` — the local auto-response (demo/playground) fields, already live via a real consumer (`packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx`). - `onSend` — the send-callback, now typed on the published authoring face rather than against the plugin's internal runtime message type. Its `messages` element is the authoring `ChatMessage` widened by the three runtime-only approval states a chat runtime hands back (objectui#10018).

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

### `.changeset/8318-jsdoc-default-tag-corrections.md`

- names `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > - `CRUDDialogSchema.size` / `.closeOnOutsideClick` / `.closeOnEscape` / `.showClose` — there is no `register('crud-dialog'` anywhere, so no node of that type ever reaches a renderer. Recorded once on the interface. Per key, the name census differs: two spellings occur nowhere outside the declaration and its zod twin, and `showClose`'s one other occurrence (`renderers/overlay/drawer.tsx:38`) belongs to `DrawerSchema`. - `ActionSchema.level` — `type: 'action'` is not a rendered node type, and `core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`, which is what makes `method` / `chainMode` / `reload` / `close` live, does not read `level`. - `CardSchema.variant` — `card` IS registered, twice, and neither registration reads it: the `ui` route forwards the key to `ui/card.tsx`, which spreads onto a `div` and mentions `variant` nowhere, and the `page` route forwards only its designer props. - `PageNodeSchema.isDefault` — `page` IS registered, and `PageRenderer` neither reads the key nor forwards it: the wrapper element gets `toDomProps(props)`, an allow-list that does not carry it.

### `.changeset/action-callback-retired-7068.md`

- names `content/docs/core/enhanced-actions.mdx` → `content/docs/core/enhanced-actions.mdx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured, on this branch's base (`900f8d99`).** `ActionCallback` (`{ type: 'toast' | 'message' | 'redirect' | 'reload' | 'custom' | 'ajax' | 'dialog', message?, url?, api?, method?, dialog?, handler? }`) was declared in `crud.ts`, mirrored in `zod/crud.zod.ts`, re-exported by both barrels, and carried on the legacy `ActionSchema` as `onSuccess?` / `onFailure?`. Producers: the package's own `phase2-schemas.test.ts` fixture and three `ts` fences in `content/docs/core/enhanced-actions.mdx` — nothing else (`git grep -l ActionCallback` over `packages content skills` hit the five `packages/types` files; positive control `SchemaNodeSchema` hit 22). Runtime readers: none — `ActionRunner` imports `UIActionSchema`, never this interface, and its own `ActionDef.onFailure` is a different (runner-native) meaning. It was the THIRD meaning of one key: objectui#5934 had already retired the runner's callback meaning of `onSuccess` and converged it on the spec's block.

### `.changeset/action-keys-warning-text-5642.md`

- names `ActionRunner.ts` → `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` — edited by this change

  > Both halves of the message's tail had outlived the change they described. It told the author the key was warned about rather than rejected because `ActionDef` "still carries `[key: string]: any`" — objectstack#4075 step 3 deleted that index signature, and `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` pins the deletion in the opposite direction (`{ ActionDef: false, ActionContext: true }`), while `actionDef-closed-surface.test.ts` pins that `tsc` now rejects exactly such a key at the construction site. And it prescribed promoting the key to an explicit field on `ActionDef` "(packages/core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts)" — that file holds the INVENTORY (`ACTION_DEF_KEYS`); the interface is in `ActionRunner.ts`. The wrong pointer had teeth: an author who followed it edited the inventory alone, which is precisely the half-change the pin test reddens on, since it re-derives the inventory from the interface's AST.

### `.changeset/tenant-header-edge-contract-5279.md`

- names `packages/auth/README.md` → `packages/auth/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `packages/auth/README.md` gains "The `X-Tenant-ID` edge contract": what the header means (a routing hint carrying the better-auth `activeOrganizationId` — not an identity claim, not an authorization input, not what scopes rows), who stamps it and under exactly which condition, who reads it, and what a reader may and may not assume. The framework half is stated as a negative with its pin — `resolveAuthzContext` takes `tenantId` from the API-key principal or `session.activeOrganizationId` and from no header — alongside `plugin-sharing`'s record that trusting `x-tenant-id` as identity *was* a vulnerability. The configuration half is quoted from the contract this package can actually resolve, `TenantRoutingConfigSchema` in `@objectstack/spec/cloud`, where `X-Tenant-ID` is the default of a configurable `tenantHeaderName` and `header` ranks second of six identification sources behind `subdomain`.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `a4fb7082a` (merge-base with origin/main): 34 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1688 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2288 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36414612185)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f6582636f9903c46023f052e1a9af7a90e2ac249`

Isolated, adversarial Clause-② review of PR objectui#10953 (card objectui#10900). Inputs: the card and its four comments (handoff `5864728339`, claim `5866735286`, dev report `5868436755`, amendment `5868466841`), the PR body, diff, file list and the head's 43 check-runs (REST), the branch at `refs/review/pr-10953` and `origin/main` (read-only), and a detached worktree of the head installed offline for targeted vitest probes. The dev report was read as a claim; every number below was re-measured.

### ① Derived judgments

**Runner translator.**
- Constructors of `ActionRunner` on the head, non-test, whole tree: `ActionProvider` (installs the translator), `useActionRunner` (installs it), the provider-less `useAction()` fallback (no translator), `ActionEngine`'s standalone branch reached by `useActionEngine` outside an `ActionProvider` (no translator; the engine installs no handlers), and the one-off `executeAction()` helper in core (no translator). The dev lists only the first two. The gap does not reach a user: `setToastHandler(` is called from exactly two non-test sites in the tree — `ActionProvider` and `useActionRunner` — so the three untranslated runners never own a toast handler and the fallback toast cannot fire through them unless a consumer installs one by hand, in which case it is English. Judged: the fallback toast translates on every path that can show it.
- Author and server text stay verbatim: the message is `dyn || action.successMessage || this.defaultSuccessToast()`; the translator is asked only inside `defaultSuccessToast()`, for the one key `actions.completedSuccessfully`. The core pin asserts `translate` is never called when a `successMessage` or a `data.message` exists. No author text can be routed through the translator.
- Language switch: `useActionRunnerTranslator` hands the runner one closure per mount that reads `latest.current` at CALL time; a dependency-less effect refreshes the ref after every render. The react pin `follows a language switch without rebuilding the runner` asserts the runner identity is unchanged across `changeLanguage('zh')` and the next toast is `操作已成功完成`. Green at head in my worktree.
- Stale closure / leak / loop: the closure holds a ref owned by the component, the effect writes a ref and no state, so no render loop; the only stale window is between a render and its commit, and actions run from events after commit. Side effect worth naming: through `useObjectTranslation` both owners now subscribe to i18next store writes (`bindI18nStore: 'added'`), so every `ActionProvider` and `useActionRunner` caller re-renders once per resource addition. A re-render, not a loop.
- Provider-less `useAction()`: the fallback runner has no toast handler, so its fallback toast never fires; a consumer that installs one on `runner` gets English. The body's "has no host, so it stays English" is honest; the fuller statement is "no toast at all unless a consumer installs a handler, then English".
- `useObjectTranslation` outside an `I18nProvider` does not throw (null context; react-i18next's not-ready `t` returns `defaultValue`), so neither owner gains a new provider requirement.
- Dependency edges: no `package.json` changed. `@object-ui/react` already depends on `@object-ui/i18n` (`workspace:*`) and imported it from non-test source on base (`index.ts`, `useActionTextLocalizer.ts` and three more), so no new chunk edge. `@object-ui/core` depends on types/formula/spec only; `@object-ui/i18n` depends on core, so the dev's "core cannot import i18n" is true and the injected seam is the right shape. `useActionRunnerTranslator` is not exported from the react entry.

**Auth.**
- Replacement hazard: `labelTemplate.replace('{provider}', …)` hands `replace` a replacer FUNCTION returning `PROVIDER_LABEL[p.id] ?? p.name`, so `$&`, `$1`, `$'` in a provider name are inserted literally; probed in node (`Acme $& Co` stays `Acme $& Co`) and pinned by the auth suite. Only the FIRST `{provider}` is replaced (string pattern); all ten packs carry exactly one hole, so nothing shipped is affected, but a pack with two holes would leave the second literal.
- The `orText` behaviour change: on base both forms computed `orText: labels.orText ?? 'or'` and read it nowhere (`l.orText` has zero reads in `LoginForm` and `RegisterForm`). A host that passed `orText` now sees it in the divider. Stated in the changeset ("documented as the divider label but rendered nowhere; it now sets the divider under the buttons") and in the body.
- Callers: the console's `LoginPage` / `RegisterPage` pass `socialButton` / `orText` with `defaultValue`; `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `LoginPage` / `RegisterPage` pass bare keys, matching their sibling labels. Four of four consistent. i18next's interpolation is `{{…}}`, so the single-brace `{provider}` survives translation, the same convention as the existing `{seconds}`.
- Default English byte-identical: base rendered `{label} {name}` as three text nodes with the same text content and accessible name as the head's one string; the divider default `'or continue with email'` is unchanged. The four en controls (`Continue with ObjectStack$`, `Sign up with ObjectStack$`, `or continue with email`) pass on base in my base run.
- Provider-name precedence (see ②): for the nine ids in `PROVIDER_LABEL` (google, github, microsoft, apple, facebook, twitter, discord, gitlab, linkedin) the component's own label is inserted whatever the server reports; `p.name` is used only for other ids, such as the card's `objectstack-cloud`. Pre-existing and unchanged by this diff.

**Build Doctor.** `aria-label`, both `title` arms and the drawer's `SheetTitle` read `console.ai.buildDoctor*` through the same `t` the neighbouring Share button already used (`ChatPane`'s `useObjectTranslation`; the drawer takes its own). `data-testid="ai-chat-debug-button"` is kept. `Build Doctor` as a literal survives on the head only in two comments and the new pin; no test or E2E selects by the English name or title. The drawer description stays an English literal, which the body declares.

**Breadcrumb.** The `AppHeader.tsx` three-dot diff is six lines, all inside the `routeType === 'system'` branch: `pathParts[3] === 'marketplace'` reads the pack, the `else if (pathParts[3])` arm keeps `humanizeSlug` for everything else, and `console.breadcrumb.system` is untouched. The console host's `system/apps`, `profile`, `approvals`, `ai-approvals`, `audit-log` and `settings` routes therefore render exactly as on base.
